title: Print Temporary Objects
prompt_md:
## Goal
Print two colors by passing temporary `Color` objects straight into a print function — without ever declaring a named `Color` variable.

## Input
One line: three integers `R G B` (0 ≤ R, G, B ≤ 255).

## Output
Two lines:
```
Default: (0, 0, 0)
Custom: (R, G, B)
```

## Task
In `main`, call the provided `printColor` twice using temporary `Color` objects constructed at the call site (lesson 14.13): once with all components 0, once with the input values. The `Color` class and `printColor` are provided — do not introduce a named `Color` variable.

title: Temporary Temperature Conversions
prompt_md:
## Goal
Use temporary `Temperature` objects two ways: pass one to a function, and call a member function directly on another — neither object gets a name.

## Input
One line: two integers `c1` and `c2` (degrees Celsius).

## Output
Two lines:
```
<c1>C = <f1>F
Quick: <f2>F
```
where each Fahrenheit value is `c * 9 / 5 + 32` using integer arithmetic.

## Task
In `main` (lesson 14.13): first call the provided `report()` with a temporary `Temperature` constructed from `c1`. Then print `Quick: ` followed by the Fahrenheit value of a second temporary `Temperature` built from `c2`, by calling `toFahrenheit()` directly on the temporary object, and finish the line with `F`. Do not declare any named `Temperature` variable. The class and `report()` are provided.
